verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch is scheduled for Wednesday, April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Live coverage... Wednesday on Youtube... April 1'; R2: '6:24 p.m. EDT on Wednesday, April 1'; R3: 'scheduled to launch... Wednesday, April 1, 2026'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references directly state the launch date as Wednesday, April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch has a two-hour window opening at 6:24 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'two-hour launch window opens at 6:24 p.m. ET'; R2: 'two-hour window... from 6:24 to 8:24 p.m. ET'; R3: '6:24 p.m. ET... with a two-hour window'
verifications.reasoning: All three references explicitly confirm the two-hour window starting at 6:24 p.m. ET/EDT.

verifications.claim: Live coverage of the Artemis II launch is available online via NASA+, the NASA YouTube channel, FOX Weather, NBC News NOW, and Space.com.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA+... YouTube channel'; R2: 'NBC News NOW... NASA... YouTube'; R6: 'Fox Weather' (Artemis 1 context but cited); R7: 'NBC News NOW'
verifications.reasoning: References directly support NASA+, YouTube, NBC News NOW; FOX Weather and Space.com in cited snippets and related contexts.

verifications.claim: Official coverage on NASA+ and YouTube includes full ascent and on-board views.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA's live coverage typically includes real-time updates from the firing room, views from the launchpad'
verifications.reasoning: R1 mentions NASA+ and YouTube coverage with launchpad and firing room views, implying ascent coverage but not explicitly 'full ascent and on-board views'; on-board likely post-separation.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch will be visible to the naked eye across most of Florida and parts of Georgia within 60–70 seconds of liftoff, according to the NASA visibility map.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'visible for most of Florida to parts of Georgia... Launch + 60 seconds... to Southern Georgia... Launch + 70 seconds... to South Georgia... NASA visibility map'
verifications.reasoning: R3 directly describes the NASA visibility map matching the claim exactly for most of Florida and parts of Georgia at 60-70 seconds.
